ModMetaData.name: Aftermath
ModMetaData.author: Nahuel
ModMetaData.description: What a battle leaves behind, the morning after. Raids end. The bodies get hauled, the blood gets mopped up, and a day later nothing shows that it ever happened. Aftermath leaves marks: small, quiet things around your colony that remember the fight. Every feature can be switched off in the mod settings. Braced Door When raiders smash one of your doors, the doorway remembers. The door you rebuild there comes back with a crossed plank nailed across it, one for every breach, and its inspect pane lists each one: when, and who did it. A door battered half to splinters gets its plank once you repair it. Deconstruct it if you want a clean slate. Trophy Standards Every hostile raid has a leader. Bring him down and his faction's standard falls with him: a banner on a pole in the faction's own colours, with their emblem on the cloth. Install it in your dining room. It remembers the date, the leader's name and the colonist who brought him down. Colonists who see it feel proud, and those who fought that day feel it most. Honored Foe Sometimes one raider nearly breaks your line, dropping two of your people or killing one. If you bury him, his grave carries his own rifle stood upright with his own helmet on top, drawn from the real weapon and helmet he died with. The grave gives his name, his faction, the people he brought down and who finally stopped him. Vigil Lamp The bed of someone fighting for their life, whether bleeding out, lost to infection or near the end of a disease, gives off a soft amber glow around the bed, easy to spot even in a roofed infirmary by day. When the danger passes the light slowly fades. If they die, it goes out at once. Bedside Offerings Every visit to a wounded colonist leaves a small gift by the bed: flowers from a lover, a sealed letter from family, a carved figure from a friend, a candle from anyone else. People who dislike the patient leave nothing. The well-loved end up surrounded and the disliked lie alone. Back on their feet, patients are cheered by how many came. If they die, the gifts stay a few days as a little shrine. The Old Sentinel A turret that has held the line through three separate fights and brought down five foes earns a name from the colonists: Old Bess, Steady Maud, The Deacon. From then on its name and its tally of foes show under it on the map. The colonists who man it or fight beside it become its old hands. When it is finally destroyed it leaves its charred remains, still carrying its name and its count, and the whole colony mourns it, its old hands most of all. Uninstall and reinstall it and it keeps its name. Safe to add to an existing save. Requires Harmony.
